questions.text: Which phase of CRISP-DM is NOT present in the original KDD process?
questions.explanation: CRISP-DM adds Business Understanding (defining the problem from a business perspective) and Deployment phases that are not explicitly in KDD. KDD starts from the data; CRISP-DM starts from the business problem.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of CRISP-DM's cyclical structure over a linear pipeline?
options: It requires fewer iterations to complete
It explicitly allows evaluation findings to loop back to earlier phases
It eliminates the need for data preparation
It guarantees deployment within a fixed timeframe
questions.explanation: CRISP-DM is explicitly cyclical — the Evaluation phase can send the project back to Data Understanding or Data Preparation if model performance reveals data quality issues or missing features.

questions.text: Which R function provides type-aware summaries including completion rates, percentiles, and inline histograms?
questions.explanation: skimr::skim() gives type-aware summaries — completion rate, percentiles for numerics, inline histograms — far more informative than base R summary() for mixed-type data.

questions.text: data.table::fread() is faster than readr::read_csv() for reading large CSV files.
questions.explanation: fread() from data.table is optimised for maximum speed, using parallel processing and memory-mapped I/O. For very large files it is typically 5–10× faster than read_csv().

questions.text: Claim amounts in the health insurance dataset are right-skewed. Which plot best reveals the shape of the bulk distribution?
options: A bar chart of plan_tier counts
A histogram on a linear x-axis
A histogram on a log10 x-axis
questions.explanation: A log10 x-axis compresses the long right tail and reveals the shape of the bulk distribution. On a linear axis the large values dominate and the structure of typical claims is invisible.
